claims.text: Low hardness and strength in equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are governed by readily activated dislocation slip combined with efficient dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery prevents substantial dislocation accumulation during deformation.
Limited dislocation accumulation suppresses work hardening.
The starting equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
The starting alloy has a uniform grain-size distribution.
The starting alloy has a low initial dislocation density.
Pre-aging can introduce secondary precipitate obstacles into CoCrFeNiTi.
Precipitates introduced by aging hinder dislocation motion.
Dynamic recovery occurs in this alloy from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures at moderate strain rates.
Easy dislocation glide in the simple solid solution promotes rapid dislocation annihilation by dynamic recovery.
Dislocation-network buildup would ordinarily increase strain hardening, hardness, and strength.
The as-cast single-phase alloy will exhibit a lower work-hardening rate than the pre-aged, precipitate-strengthened alloy under identical loading.
The as-cast single-phase alloy will exhibit a lower steady-state dislocation density than the pre-aged alloy.
The as-cast single-phase alloy will have lower hardness and strength than the pre-aged, precipitate-strengthened alloy.
Very low temperatures or extremely high strain rates may suppress dynamic recovery and therefore fall outside the hypothesis boundary.
A robust increase in dislocation density and work hardening in the as-cast alloy, similar to or greater than that in the aged control, would falsify dynamic recovery as the dominant mechanism.
